source_text:
Γρηγορεῖτε ὑπὲρ τῆς ζωῆς ὑμῶν: οἱ λύχνοι ὑμῶν μὴ σβεσθήτωσαν, καὶ αἱ ὀσφύες ὑμῶν μὴ ἐκλυέσθωσαν, ἀλλὰ γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι: οὐ γὰρ οἴδατε τὴν ὤραν, ἐν ᾗ ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν ἔρχεται.
πυκνῶς δὲ συναχθήσεσθε ζητοῦντες τὰ ἀνήκοντα ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν: οὐ γὰρ ὠφελήσει ὑμᾶς ὁ πᾶς χρόνος τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν, ἐὰν μὴ ἐν τῷ ἐσχάτῳ καιρῷ τελειωθῆτε.
ἐν γὰρ ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις πληθυνθήσονται οἱ ψευδοπροφῆται καὶ οἱ φθορεῖς, καὶ στραφήσονται τὰ πρόβατα εἰς λύκους, καὶ ἡ ἀγάπη στραφήσεται εἰς μῖσος.
αὐξανούσης γὰρ τῆς ἀνομίας μισήσουσιν ἀλλήλους καὶ διώξουσι καὶ παραδώσουσι, καὶ τότε φανήσεται ὁ κοσμοπλανὴς ὡς υἱὸς θεοῦ, καὶ ποιήσει σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα, καὶ ἡ γῆ παραδοθήσεται εἰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ, καὶ ποιήσει ἀθέμιτα, ἅ οὐδέποτε γέγονεν ἐξ αἰῶνος.
τότε ἥξει ἡ κτίσις τῶν ἀνθρώπων εἰς τὴν πύρωσιν τῆς δοκιμασίας, καὶ σκανδαλισθήσονται πολλοὶ καὶ ἀπολοῦνται, οἱ δὲ ὑπομείναντες ἐν τῇ πίστει αὐτῶν σωθήσονται ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ καταθέματος.
καὶ τότε φανήσεται τὰ σημεῖα τῆς ἀληθείας: πρῶτον σημεῖον ἐκπετάσεως ἐν οὐρανῷ, εἶτα σημεῖον φωνῆς σάλπιγγος, καὶ τὸ τρίτον ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν.
οὐ πάντων δέ, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐρρέθη: Ἥξει ὁ κύριος καὶ πάντες οἱ ἅγιοι μετ’ αὐτοῦ.
τότε ὄψεται ὁ κόσμος τὸν κύριον ἐρχόμενον ἐπάνω τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
orientation: The Didache closes with an apocalyptic exhortation: the community is to stay awake and ready, because the Lord will come at an unknown hour, and the final days will bring false prophets, the world-deceiver, and a testing by fire before the Lord appears on the clouds.
pass_a_gloss: Be watchful over your life: your lamps let them not be quenched, and your loins let them not be loosened (an idiom meaning 'stay ready / be prepared'), but become ready: for you do not know the hour, in which our Lord comes. And frequently you shall be gathered together seeking the things that belong to your souls: for the whole time of your faith will not benefit you, if not in the last season you are made perfect. For in the last days the false prophets and the corrupters will be multiplied, and the sheep will be turned into wolves, and love will be turned into hatred. For when lawlessness increases they will hate one another and will persecute and will hand over, and then the deceiver of the world will appear as a son of God, and he will do signs and wonders, and the earth will be handed over into his hands, and he will do unlawful things, which never have happened from the age. Then the creation of humans will come into the burning of the testing, and many will be made to stumble and will perish, but the ones who have remained under in their faith will be saved by the curse itself. And then the signs of the truth will appear: first a sign of spreading out in heaven, then a sign of a voice of a trumpet, and the third a resurrection of dead ones. Not of all, but as it was said: The Lord will come and all the holy ones with him. Then the world will see the Lord coming upon the clouds of heaven.

choices.why: The glossary fixed this rendering for κοσμοπλανής; it keeps the genitive force of 'world' as the object of deception.
The phrase is odd and emphatic; 'the curse itself' preserves the article and the strange agency, which is likely a reference to Christ as the accursed one (cf. Gal 3:13).
The noun suggests an opening or unfolding, likely of the heavens; 'spreading out' keeps the physical image without over-interpreting.
The passive voice and the sense of completion at the end time are both important; 'made perfect' preserves the passive and the eschatological nuance.
καιρός is a season or appointed time, not a clock-time; 'last season' keeps the eschatological sense distinct from 'hour' (ὥρα) earlier in the passage.

pass_b_english: Stay awake for the sake of your lives. Do not let your lamps go out, and do not let your loins be loosened. Be ready, because you do not know the hour when our Lord is coming (Matthew 24:42).
Gather together frequently, and seek what is fitting for your souls. The whole time of your faith will not help you unless you are made perfect at the last season.
For in the last days the false prophets and the corrupters will multiply, and the sheep will be turned into wolves, and love will be turned into hatred.

For as lawlessness increases, people will hate one another and persecute one another and betray one another. Then the deceiver of the world will appear as a son of God, and he will perform signs and wonders, and the earth will be handed over into his hands, and he will do unlawful things such as have never happened from eternity.
Then the creation of human beings will enter the fire of testing, and many will be made to stumble and will perish. But those who endure in their faith will be saved from that very accursed one.
And then the signs of the truth will appear: first, a sign of spreading out in heaven; then, a sign of a trumpet's voice; and the third, the resurrection of the dead.
Not of all, however, but as it was said: The Lord will come, and all the holy ones with him (cf. Zechariah 14:5).
Then the world will see the Lord coming on the clouds of heaven (Matthew 24:30).

problems.why: The Greek says 'by the curse itself' but contextually this must mean 'by him the accursed one' or 'by that very condemned one' referring to the deceiver; 'curse itself' makes no sense as savior.

edits.old: will be saved by the curse itself.
edits.new: will be saved by that very accursed one.

problems.source_quote: οὐ γὰρ οἴδατε τὴν ὤραν, ἐν ᾗ ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν ἔρχεται
problems.why: The citation should be Matthew 24:42,44 or Mark 13:35; but the Greek matches Matthew 24:42 closely ("οὐκ οἴδατε ποίᾳ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ κύριος ὑμῶν ἔρχεται"). However, the exact phrase "τὴν ὤραν" appears in Matthew 24:42. This is actually correct.

problems.quote: will be saved by that very accursed one
problems.why: "ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ καταθέματος" means "from that very accursed one" or "by him the accursed one" - but contextually the deceiver is the threat, not savior. The Greek is ambiguous but likely means saved FROM him or despite him.
problems.fix: will be saved from that very accursed one

edits.old: will be saved by that very accursed one
edits.new: will be saved from that very accursed one

fixed: The citation (Matthew 24:42) is correct and matches the Greek source closely; no change needed.

problems.quote: The Lord will come, and all the holy ones with him (Zechariah 14:5)
problems.why: Zechariah 14:5 does not contain this phrase; it says the Lord will be king over all the earth.
problems.fix: Either cite the correct verse or re‑phrase to match the actual passage.

edits.old: The Lord will come, and all the holy ones with him (Zechariah 14:5).
edits.new: The Lord will come, and all the holy ones with him.

fixed: Removed the incorrect Zechariah 14:5 citation; the source does not identify a specific scriptural reference for this quotation.

problems.quote: The Lord will come, and all the holy ones with him.
problems.why: Presented as scripture ('as it was said') but no speaker or source identified.

problems.quote: The Lord will come, and all the holy ones with him.
problems.why: No citation given; echoes Zechariah 14:5, not identified for reader.

edits.old: The Lord will come, and all the holy ones with him.
edits.new: The Lord will come, and all the holy ones with him (cf. Zechariah 14:5).

problems.quote: You, Almighty Master, created all things
problems.why: Same referent (God) given three different titles; reader may think 'Almighty Master' is a different divine figure.
problems.fix: Note that 'Almighty Master' is an epithet for God the Father.

problems.quote: do not let your loins go slack
problems.why: Idiomatic for 'stay alert' but reads strangely in modern English; reader may be confused.
problems.fix: Gloss: an idiom meaning 'stay ready / be prepared.'

edits.old: do not let your loins go slack
edits.new: do not let your loins be loosened

fixed: The glossary problem about 'Almighty Master' is not present in this section; no edit needed.
The unreadable idiom 'do not let your loins go slack' was adjusted to match the source more closely while retaining the idiomatic sense.

last_rejected.why: Source alludes to 1 Thess 4:16–17, not Matthew 24.
last_rejected.fix: Remove parenthetical or correct reference; no Matthew citation applies here.
last_rejected.ruling: Claim misidentifies issue: 'ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν' is literal translation, not wrong scripture reference. English cites no verse here.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ἥξει ὁ κύριος καὶ πάντες οἱ ἅγιοι μετ’ αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: The source quotes 'The Lord will come, and all the holy ones with him'—this matches Zechariah 14:5 in the LXX (ἥξει κύριος ὁ θεός μου καὶ πάντες οἱ ἅγιοι μετ' αὐτοῦ). However, this exact wording also appears in 1 Thessalonians 3:13 and is alluded to in Matthew 24:30-31. The brief notes 'quotes material resembling Malachi 1:11 and/or 1:14 in section 14' but does not specify this verse. The citation is plausible but the English adds a specific verse reference where the source has none; this is an editorial addition not in the source.
last_rejected.fix: Remove '(Zechariah 14:5)' or verify; the source presents the quotation without identifying its scriptural source.
last_rejected.ruling: Source words match Zech 14:5 LXX closely; citation is a plausible editorial identification, not a meaning-changing error.

last_rejected.source_quote: τότε ὄψεται ὁ κόσμος τὸν κύριον ἐρχόμενον ἐπάνω τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ
last_rejected.why: The source presents this as the author's own concluding statement, not as a marked scriptural citation. The English adds '(Matthew 24:30)' where the source has no citation marker. While the wording resembles Matthew 24:30, the source integrates it as part of the author's eschatological description without attributing it to Scripture.
last_rejected.fix: Remove '(Matthew 24:30)'; the source presents this as authorial statement, not marked citation.
last_rejected.ruling: Source words ἐρχόμενον ἐπάνω τῶν νεφελῶν match Matt 24:30; editorial reference is plausible, not misleading.

polish.changed: Clarified pronoun references, smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud, and made the implied subjects explicit without altering any claims or Scripture references.

notes.quote: the deceiver of the world will appear as a son of God, and he will perform signs and wonders
notes.why: Suggests the Antichrist is a literal Son of God, contrary to early‑church understanding.
notes.fix: Rephrase to “will appear as a false messiah”.
